hypothesis: Flyweight's sharing law is expressible on the current kernel surface after all: a declarative key on the flyweight object indexes the intrinsic tuple (one shared instance per intrinsic state; any two colliding rows are one executed violation each), and a path equation names the client's handle as the factory's instance for its key. The prior disposition ('identity is data; no predicate') is refuted for structural sharing. The hypothesis under test is the P6 parity hypothesis: the kernel buys zero unique detections over the complete conventional Flyweight test.

F-Intern.name: one shared instance per intrinsic state
F-Intern.statement: for the declared instance, `intrinsic: Flyweight -> Intrinsic` is injective over the flyweight rows: no two distinct flyweight rows carry the same intrinsic tuple
F-Intern.surface: format 1.3 declarative key {object: Flyweight, arrows: [intrinsic], status: accepted}; every colliding unordered pair is one executed `violation` with witness {key, rows}
F-Intern.why: the key is an injectivity predicate over declared rows; it needs no notion of runtime object identity, only the declared intrinsic cells

F-Handle.name: the client's handle is the factory's instance for its key
F-Handle.statement: for every declared client c, flyweight(c) = factory(key(c)) as a row co-reference (dense row id), not a value comparison
F-Handle.surface: path equation lhs [key, factory] / rhs [flyweight] over Client -> Flyweight
F-Handle.why: the equation compares the two paths' target row ids, so it is a co-reference predicate; equal intrinsic values in different rows are still a violation

F-Closure.name: every declared flyweight instance is the factory's image (no leaked instance)
F-Closure.statement: every declared Flyweight row is in the image of `factory`
F-Closure.surface: none — the kernel has no surjectivity/closure predicate; `query --follow factory --direction backward` can compute the preimage, but a query result is data, never a finding
F-Closure.missing_predicate: a surjectivity / image-closure predicate on a declared arrow over declared rows (or an unreachable-instance finding)
F-Closure.why: declarative keys state injectivity only; equations relate path values from the same source row; the analysis ops return data (closures, questions) and emit no finding for a declared-but-unreachable row

F-Capacity.name: declared instance counts and share counts
F-Capacity.statement: the number of flyweight instances, or the share count of one intrinsic state, obeys a declared bound
F-Capacity.surface: none — colliding *pairs* are observable through F-Intern, but no numeric/cardinality predicate exists over row counts
F-Capacity.missing_predicate: an arithmetic/cardinality constraint over declared instance counts (e.g. max instances per intrinsic state, or a declared pool size)
F-Capacity.why: the closed constraint vocabulary is path equality, totality, injectivity keys, and presentation rules; none carries a numeral over instance counts. F-Intern gives pair existence, not counts

comparison_rule: An element is one named witness both arms may identify: `flyweight:handle-identity@Client#<idx>` (a client whose handle differs from the factory's instance for its key), `flyweight:interning-pair@Flyweight#<lo>/Flyweight#<hi>` (an unordered colliding pair, ascending), or `flyweight:pool-closure@Flyweight#<idx>` (a declared instance the factory cannot return). The probe arm maps an executed `violation` witness to exactly one element: an equation witness {equation: 0, row: r} maps to the handle element of Client#r; a key witness {key: 0, rows: [lo, hi]} maps to the interning-pair element. unique = probe elements minus baseline elements; the baseline's pool-closure elements have no probe counterpart by construction (F-Closure is unexpressible), so they can never be unique.
